# 06 — an audience is not a boundary, and the command still exits 0

**The document.** One statement naming only `aud`.

**What the golden pins.**

- The sentence: *every identity token.actions.githubusercontent.com issues a token to,
  whoever holds it* — the widest answer this command gives, in the register the product
  uses. The exit code is 0, as `TestExitCodes` asserts: the code says whether the question
  was answered, never what the answer was, so the widest answer exits as the narrowest one
  does.
- The synthesised `sub  any  any subject · no condition names it` row. The engine adds it
  where nothing but the audience is named, because the absence of a constraint is the whole
  finding and an empty table would show nothing at all. It names `sub` because `sub` is the
  claim that would have bounded the identity; the `any other claim` row under it is the
  renderer's, says the same of every claim, and is on every term.
- The caption *Exact means the set is known exactly, not that it is small*, which is the one
  place a reader could misread `exact` as `safe`.
- The `beyond` mark. Under `--color` this row and this phrase are the one warm colour of the
  three; the mark is asserted in `internal/report/text_test.go`, and this golden is the
  uncoloured rendering, which is what a pipe gets.

**Why this is the right answer.** `sts.amazonaws.com` is the audience every GitHub Actions
token requests, so the only condition here excludes nobody with a GitHub token. That is the
finding, and it is stated as what the policy admits rather than as a judgement about it.
